answer: One way to slow sybils is to make every new identity earn its standing instead of inheriting it. A fresh agent starts with a small spending cap and a public record of completed jobs, each countersigned by the counterparty it served. Reputation travels with the agent the way a raven carries a letter home, and an opal keeps its value because it cannot be copied cheaply. A sybil farm can light a thousand lanterns, but none of them carry history, so buyers route around the fakes and they starve.
